text.p: National-Standard Co said it will close its Knoxville, Tenn., facility and transfer production of wire cloth for the air bag industry to its Corbin, Ky., and Clearfield, Utah, plants.
National-Standard said the consolidation of manufacturing operations will increase the profitability of its Woven Filter Fiber Division in light of declining prices.

The Knoxville location, which opened in 1993, currently has 57 full-time employees and 46 temporary employees who are primarily involved in the production of materials used in automotive air bag filters. The plant will close August 1.

"National-Standard has made a difficult business decision to close our Knoxville facility, but believe it is in the best interest of our customers and our shareholders," Mike Savitske, chief executive officer, said in a statement issued Tuesday. "Streamlining production will help us to better serve our customers and significantly reduce overhead costs."
